elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or eligible Service Option Attachments for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may make the convenience termination effective on 30 days' notice without an additional timing restriction.
elements.evidence: Termination is permitted only at the end of a calendar month and requires at least one month's prior notice. Depending on the notice date, Customer may have to wait materially longer than 30 days.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (a) expressly requires prior written notice.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: IBM must refund any charges prepaid for the period after the effective termination date, which operatively provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination is not subject to an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Paragraph (b) preserves the applicable early-termination charges, subject only to a three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative clause grants a convenience-termination right only to Customer and contains no IBM convenience-termination right.
The clause expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate on a notice period no less favorable to Customer than 60–90 days.
elements.evidence: Customer can select a calendar-month-end termination date falling within 60–90 days after notice, and the clause may permit an earlier month-end date because its minimum notice requirement is only one month.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The aggregate early-termination charges are expressly capped at three months' charges for the terminated Services.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination-for-convenience right is exercisable only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted in the supplied operative clause, so the condition requiring this restriction is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted in the supplied operative clause, so the condition requiring a 90-day notice provision is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback because Customer retains a convenience-termination right on timing no less favorable than the fallback range, early-termination charges are capped at three months, and IBM receives no convenience-termination right. It does not reach the preferred position because termination remains limited to calendar month-end and remains subject to early-termination charges. The changes preserve the clause's unrelated scope and dependency exception without contradiction. The redline is not strictly minimal to the completed fallback level because the prepaid-fee refund, although favorable and related to the preferred position, was not necessary to satisfy the fallback.
